overview.title: 📖 Overview: Fences, a Hard Dilemma, and a New Mishna
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 13a–13b
overview.hebrewSource: וְאֶל אִשָּׁה בְּנִדַּת טוּמְאָתָהּ לֹא תִקְרָב
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf extends the mishna's concern about a zav eating with a zava into a further rabbinic fence, and then takes up a difficult dilemma: may a menstruating woman (niddah) share a bed with her husband if both remain fully clothed? After weighing several proofs, the Gemara settles the question from a verse in Ezekiel and tells a sobering story about a scholar who died young for treating the law too lightly. The daf then opens the new mishna describing the eighteen decrees issued in the attic of Ḥananya ben Ḥizkiya ben Garon, including the story of Megillat Ta'anit and the start of the list of decrees disqualifying teruma.

slides.title: 🚫 A Fence Around a Fence — Whom May a Zav Eat With?
slides.subtitle: Extending the mishna's ban beyond the zav and zava themselves

lines.speaker: Mishna
lines.text: A zav may not eat with a zava, lest familiarity lead to sin — 'come and see how far purity spread in Israel,' since even two who are both impure may not share a meal.

lines.speaker: Extension
lines.text: A scrupulous zav (parush) may also not eat with a zav who is an am ha'aretz, lest the am ha'aretz get him used to spending time together.

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: The concern is that the am ha'aretz will feed him untithed produce.

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: Most amei ha'aretz do tithe their produce — rather, the concern is that he'll grow accustomed to the am ha'aretz and, even after his own purity returns, be fed impure food.

slides.title: 🛌 May a Niddah and Her Husband Share a Bed, Both Clothed?
slides.subtitle: Rav Yosef's dilemma, tested against two mishnayot, then settled

nodes.content: ❓ Rav Yosef's dilemma: may a menstruating woman sleep beside her husband, she in her clothes and he in his?
🧀 First attempt: the fowl-with-cheese mishna — rejected, since one table means one mind, unlike two people who each keep their own awareness
🍖 Second attempt: two guests eating meat and cheese at one table — also rejected, since there is no visible reminder there, while sleeping fully dressed is itself an unusual, noticeable change

columns.label: Ezekiel 18:6
columns.content: Juxtaposes 'a woman in her impurity' with 'his neighbor's wife' — just as clothed contact with a forbidden married woman is prohibited, so is clothed contact with a niddah wife

columns.label: Rabbi Pedat (dissent)
columns.content: The Torah forbade only intimacy that constitutes actual forbidden relations (Leviticus 18:6) — mere affectionate contact is not included

slides.title: 💔 'Blessed Is the One Who Killed Him' — Eliyahu's Story
slides.subtitle: A cautionary tale about honoring the law of niddah
slides.hebrewSource: וְאֶל אִשָּׁה בְּנִדַּת טוּמְאָתָהּ לֹא תִקְרָב
slides.label: The story:
slides.text: A devoted student, who studied and served Torah scholars extensively, died at half his years. His grieving widow told Eliyahu that during her days of impurity her husband never touched her, not even with his little finger — but during her 'white days,' after the bleeding stopped and before her immersion, they ate, drank, and slept together with bodily contact, with no further intent. Eliyahu answered: 'Blessed is the Omnipresent who killed him, for he showed no honor to the Torah' — since 'you shall not approach a woman in her menstrual impurity' (Leviticus 18:19) forbids even affectionate contact, not only relations. Rav Dimi later clarified this meant sleeping in one bed without actual touching; in the West they said a sinar (belt) separated them — yet since even that remained prohibited, he was held responsible.

slides.title: 📜 Megillat Ta'anit and the Attic of Ḥananya ben Ḥizkiya
slides.subtitle: The mishna's introduction to the eighteen decrees
rows: Ḥananya ben Ḥizkiya and his faction, who cherished the memory of Israel's troubles and salvations
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: they are too numerous to write; also, 'a madman does not feel his own wound,' and 'dead flesh does not feel the scalpel' — only pain still felt gets recorded
He saved the book of Ezekiel from suppression — its contents seemed to contradict Torah law — sitting isolated with 300 jugs of oil until he resolved every contradiction
What happened that day in his attic?
Sages gathered to visit him; when counted, Beit Shammai's students outnumbered Beit Hillel's, and eighteen decrees were issued following Beit Shammai's opinion

slides.title: 📋 The Eighteen Decrees Begin: What Disqualifies Teruma
slides.subtitle: Items that render teruma unfit without transmitting further impurity

steps.content: 1️⃣ One who ate food with first- or second-degree ritual impurity disqualifies teruma he touches — but (per Rabbi Yehoshua) does not transmit further impurity onward
2️⃣ One who drinks impure liquids, or whose head and majority of his body entered drawn water right after immersing
3️⃣ A pure person on whom three log of drawn water fell; a Torah scroll; unwashed hands; one who immersed but still awaits nightfall
4️⃣ Foods and vessels that became impure through contact with certain liquids — the list the Gemara now works through case by case

summary.principle: The daf shows the Sages building careful fences around potential sin — extending the zav-and-zava rule further, and, in the graver matter of niddah, ruling that even fully clothed contact is forbidden — before opening the mishna's list of eighteen decrees safeguarding the purity of teruma.

flowSteps.content: 🚫 A scrupulous zav may not even eat with an am ha'aretz zav, lest habit lead him astray later
❓ May a niddah share a bed with her husband, both clothed? Two proofs tried and rejected

columns.content: 🛌 Settled from Ezekiel 18:6: even clothed contact is forbidden
💔 A student's early death illustrates the cost of treating this lightly

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Ḥananya ben Ḥizkiya's attic produced eighteen decrees safeguarding teruma's purity, following Beit Shammai's majority that day

quiz.q: Why does Rava, against Abaye, permit a scrupulous zav to eat with an am ha'aretz zav on the grounds of tithing?
o: Because tithing laws do not apply during impurity
Because most amei ha'aretz do in fact tithe their produce — Rava's real concern is different
Because Rava rejects the concept of am ha'aretz entirely
Because the zav is exempt from all dietary concerns
quiz.e: Rava holds that most amei ha'aretz tithe, so untithed food is not the concern; instead he worries the zav will grow accustomed to the am ha'aretz and later be fed impure food even after regaining his own purity.

quiz.q: What verse does the Gemara ultimately use to prove that a niddah may not share a bed with her husband even while both are clothed?
o: Leviticus 18:6, on forbidden relatives
Ezekiel 18:6, which juxtaposes a niddah with 'his neighbor's wife'
Exodus 31:13, on the Shabbat as a sign
Deuteronomy 30:20, 'for it is your life'
quiz.e: The Gemara reasons from the juxtaposition in Ezekiel 18:6: just as clothed contact with a forbidden married woman is prohibited, so is clothed contact with a niddah wife.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Pedat, what does the Torah actually prohibit with regard to forbidden relatives?
o: Any conversation with them
Only intimacy that constitutes actual forbidden relations, not mere affectionate contact
Living in the same household as them
Nothing — Rabbi Pedat holds there is no prohibition at all
quiz.e: Rabbi Pedat holds the Torah's prohibition (Leviticus 18:6) covers only actual sexual relations, disagreeing with the Gemara's stricter conclusion from Ezekiel about mere contact.

quiz.q: According to Eliyahu's account, why did the devoted student die at half his years?
o: He neglected his Torah study
He maintained bodily contact with his wife during her 'white days,' before her immersion, showing insufficient honor to the Torah's prohibition
He failed to give charity
He disrespected his teachers
quiz.e: Even though he never touched his wife during her actual niddah days, he slept with bodily contact during the days she was counting toward immersion — which Eliyahu says still violates the Torah's prohibition of approaching a niddah.

quiz.q: Who wrote Megillat Ta'anit, and why, according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, did they not record every day of trouble Israel experienced?
o: Moses wrote it, and left days out due to lack of space on the scroll
Ḥananya ben Ḥizkiya and his faction wrote it, and there were simply too many such days to record them all
The Men of the Great Assembly wrote it, omitting days that were later forgotten
It was written anonymously, omitting days still under dispute
quiz.e: Ḥananya ben Ḥizkiya and his faction, who cherished the memory of Israel's troubles and salvations, wrote the scroll — but Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel explained that the troubles of every generation are too numerous to record in full.
